rule_level_problems.problem: 'Shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) has no probable Shock rule, so shock in the red box depends entirely on a worker recording 'Shock'.

Exposure is modelled only as travel history; residents of malaria areas (the page says 'in a malaria area') are not captured. The 3-month window relies on the onset of a history-of-travel situation, which only works if the worker records the travel date.

rule_level_problems.problem: The danger-sign list is copied verbatim into both rules instead of the priority rule referencing (diagnosis Complicated malaria possible); correct now, but the copies can drift apart. The anuria clause relies on a back-dated onset (>= 12 hours ago), which may never be true when anuria is first recorded at triage.

summary: The red box is complete: all 11 representable danger signs are encoded with correct concepts and thresholds in an Urgent rule anchored on possible malaria, plus a matching possible Complicated (severe) malaria rule. Hb < 7 is rightly left out as not representable. The most consequential gap is footnote 2's 'shock likely', which has no probable Shock rule. The suspect-malaria rule is partial: exposure is encoded as travel history only, which misses people who live in malaria areas, and its 3-month window depends on the recorded onset of the travel history.
